claims.disposition: Verified from complete source at sha256:31ef6a15. bus.rs:706-708 is the field rustdoc, :709 is `maintenance_gate: Arc<Mutex<MaintenanceGate>>`, :710 is the struct close. Her 709-710 span covers the field plus the closing brace; the field itself is line 709. Access is always via lock_maintenance_gate (:727-738), which fails closed on a poisoned mutex by forcing blocked=true and exact=false.

claims.summary: The documentation for set_user_input_blocked states that it blocks all new IPC IpcPayload::UserInput events at the kernel bus boundary.
claims.disposition: Quote verified verbatim at bus.rs:760-761. Scope corrected without narrowing her concern: enforcement in admits_while_blocked (:71-123) is broader than that doc line. UserInput is the one unconditional deny (:73); AgentResponse, LlmRequest, LlmStreamEvent, LlmResponse, ToolExecuteRequest, ToolExecuteResult and ToolCancelRequest are admitted only when bound to an already-tracked trace/call; the catch-all (:121) admits everything else.

claims.summary: The existence of publish_maintenance_barrier (778-812) suggests a specialized way to interact with the bus during blocked states.
claims.disposition: Verified and strengthened. It is the only producer that requires blocked: :812-819 returns None unless blocked && exact && zero active conversations, llm requests and tools. It bypasses `publish` entirely, sending on self.sender directly (:842), so admits_while_blocked never applies to it, and it stamps a kernel_host/maintenance_gate producer (:832-835). Its payload names itself a drain barrier, not action authority (:828).

claims.summary: Her stated question: does EventBus perform a synchronous check and drop the message (returning an error or None), or is the interaction more complex?
claims.disposition: Answered from complete source. publish (:890-948) takes the maintenance_gate mutex once (:894) and gates admission under the same lock as the activity accounting, so no drained snapshot can be observed between them (:891-893). A rejected IPC message logs at debug and returns 0 (:899-900) — not an Err, not a None: the signature returns usize. It is synchronous and terminal; nothing queues, delays or retries it.

claims.summary: Steward finding from her reading: a zero return from publish was treated as equivalent to 'the message is discarded', and nothing pinned the difference.
claims.disposition: Implemented. Zero is ambiguous by construction: an admitted event with no async receivers also returns 0 (:926-941) yet still reaches every synchronous registry subscriber (:945), while a gate-rejected event reaches neither. The difference is reach, not return value. Added regression publish_zero_separates_gate_rejection_from_absent_async_receivers and corrected the publish rustdoc, which previously described only the async-receiver count.
